text:
Zayne Parekh is 20 and already arguing with the rulebook. Sportsnaut's headline says it plainly: "Zayne Parekh Is Challenging One of Hockey's Oldest Positional Rules." The Flames' 2024 ninth overall pick is a defenseman who plays like a forward, and Calgary is giving him 18:37 a night.

He has 11 points in 26 games, 5 on the power play, which is 0.42 a game against a median of 0.25 for defensemen picked in his range in their first full season. He shoots plenty (47 shots) and the Flames win 51.8% of the expected goals (chance quality) at five on five with him, about six points better than without him. If anything, he's been unlucky: 2 goals on 3.9 expected.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, in a small sample, calls him a setup man (86th percentile in primary shot assists) who exits the zone cleanly. This is the player who scored 96 points in 66 OHL games and 13 in 7 at the World Juniors. The Win Column asked, "Is Zayne Parekh already a top defenceman in the NHL?" We'd say not yet. But the path is visible.
headline: Parekh is ahead of the curve
